title: Aurum Alpha upload policy
description: standards/026-blob-storage.md BS6: the declaration a service carries in its repository stating, per entity that owns objects, what may be uploaded - the admitted content types, the size ceiling, whether the object is scanned before it is served, how it is served, and the read and intent lifetimes. The server reads it at intent time and at confirm; a reviewer reads it to see the service's exposure in one file. An entity with no entry accepts no uploads. Two rules prose states are decidable here and are: an object other people download is scanned (BS7), and a presigned read never outlives the ceiling (BS5). schema_version 1 - evolves additively per PC6.

duration.description: ISO 8601 duration, days and time components only, in the form 057's declaration uses.

readTtl.description: BS5. The lifetime of a presigned GET, bounded above by the ceiling of one hour: PT<n>S up to 3600, PT<n>M up to 60, or PT1H. A longer value does not validate, because a presigned URL is a bearer credential and its lifetime is the only revocation it has.

inlineSafeType.description: BS5. The media types a browser may be told to render inline. Excluded on purpose: image/svg+xml and text/html, which carry script; anything the browser would sniff into one of those.

entityPolicy.description: BS6. The upload rules for one entity, keyed by the entity segment of the object key (key.schema.json).

max_size_bytes.description: BS6. The largest object this entity accepts. Checked against the declared size at intent, before a presign is issued, and against the size storage reports at confirm.

content_types.description: BS6. The closed set of media types this entity admits, each a full type/subtype. The declared type at intent must be in it and the sniffed type at confirm must equal the declared one.

audience.description: BS7. Who reads what is uploaded here. uploader: only the person who uploaded it ever receives a presigned read - a profile photo shown back to its owner, an export a user requested. others: anyone else may - an attachment on a shared record, a document sent to a client. others requires scan: true.

scan.description: BS7. Whether an object is scanned for malware before a presigned read is issued. Required true where audience is others; where false, every object of this entity is scan: not_required.

disposition.description: BS5. How the server sets Content-Disposition on every presigned read. attachment is the default and the safe one; inline is admitted only where every admitted content type is in the inline-safe list.

retention.description: BS8. Present only where a domain reason keeps objects past the life of the owning row, in the manner 025 SD12 admits soft delete. States the reason and the period; the object stays scoped and erasable for the whole of it.

reason.description: The domain or statutory reason, in a sentence a reviewer can check.

period.description: How long past the owning row's deletion the object is kept.

allOf.description: BS7. What one person uploads for another to download is scanned before it is served.
BS5. inline only over types a browser renders without executing.

schema_version.description: PC6. The version of this shape.

tenant_scoped.description: BS3, BS10. Whether object keys carry the tenant segment. true for any service with a tenant isolation level (025 SD5); false only for a service that has none.

presign_get_ttl.description: BS5. The lifetime of every presigned GET this service issues. Default PT15M; ceiling PT1H, enforced by the pattern. A caller may ask for shorter and never for longer.

intent_ttl.description: BS6, BS8. How long a pending intent row waits for its confirm before the purge job treats it as abandoned: deletes the object if one arrived, and the row. Default PT1H.

multipart_threshold_bytes.description: BS6. Above this declared size the intent returns a multipart upload rather than a single presigned PUT. Bounded below by the S3 API's minimum part size of five mebibytes and above by its single-PUT ceiling of five gibibytes. Default 104857600 (one hundred mebibytes).

entities.description: BS6. One entry per entity that owns objects, keyed by the entity segment of the key. An entity absent here accepts no uploads.
